extracted.intended_audience: academics and researchers (especially early-career) asked to peer-review journal manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing peer review of scholarly manuscripts: deciding whether to accept a review, conducting an initial skim, identifying major flaws, doing a section-by-section critique, and writing a professional, constructive review with a clear recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient expertise to review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before accepting, ensure you have the necessary expertise to evaluate the manuscript's topic and methods. If not, decline so editors can find alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine interest in the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept only if you have a substantive interest in the topic; lack of interest may lead to a low-quality review or unnecessary delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and disclose any relationships or financial conflicts that could bias your review. If a conflict exists, decline promptly so the editor can seek another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time availability / turnaround
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm you can meet the expected turnaround (the page cites ~10 days). If you cannot, decline quickly to allow the editor to find alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: First reading — identify central research question and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Skim for: Central research question and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On first read, be able to state the central question and judge whether the study addresses an important problem or gap in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: First reading — originality and field contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Skim for: Originality and field contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work offers novel insights or advances the field, or whether it is incremental or redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: First reading — conclusions should match evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the authors' conclusions are supported by the data and analyses presented; flag overreaching claims on first pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: First reading — figures and tables necessary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether each figure/table is necessary and whether it communicates the data clearly; note any missing or superfluous displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: First reading — look for major flaws
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any obvious, potentially fatal problems early so you can decide whether a deeper review is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — conclusion contradicted by evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag cases where the stated conclusions are not supported by the presented results or where interpretation conflicts with the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — outdated or discredited methodology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify use of methods that the field has moved beyond or that are known to be invalid for the question; explain why the method is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — overlooked influential factors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note missing confounders, covariates, or key literature/variables that would change interpretation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — weak, ambiguous, or inconsistent data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out data quality problems, ambiguous measurements, or internal inconsistencies across datasets or analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — weak statistical support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether statistical analyses are appropriate and adequately powered; flag misuse of tests, p-hacking, or unsupported inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — redundant data without novelty
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note if the manuscript simply repeats previously published results or includes data that do not add new insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major flaw — poor writing clarity and numerous errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify pervasive clarity or language problems that impede understanding; specify examples and suggest fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed section-by-section review
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine each component (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References, Acknowledgements) separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a component-wise critique (the page provides a downloadable checklist with section-specific questions). Check that the Introduction frames the question, Methods are detailed and reproducible, Results are clear, Discussion is balanced, References are appropriate, and Acknowledgements disclose support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening paragraph of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening paragraph: summarize the research, demonstrate comprehension, highlight strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin by succinctly summarizing the manuscript and its main findings to show you understood the work; also briefly note key strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body of the review — cover contribution, methods, data, novelty, and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Body: contribution, methodology, data, novelty; concerns clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the main body, evaluate the study's contribution, rigor of methodology, quality of data, and novelty. List specific concerns and required revisions, with clear explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation with rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation: Accept / Major / Minor Revision / Reject with rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear recommendation and justify it with reference to major and minor issues. Editors rely on this summary to make decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag fraud or plagiarism separately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you detect potential fraud or plagiarism, alert the editor explicitly and separately from routine critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat reviewing as a serious professional responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat reviewing as a serious professional responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach reviews conscientiously and timely; recognize peer review as part of scholarly service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate scientific rigor and clarity, not potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate scientific rigor and clarity, not potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on methodological soundness and clarity of presentation rather than speculating about future influence or 'impact'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive suggestions and avoid excessive criticism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critiques to help authors improve the work. Be specific about how to fix issues; avoid gratuitous negative language that doesn't aid revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific line/page references
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to precise locations (line, page, figure) when identifying problems so authors and editors can quickly find them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral language — focus on the work, not the authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Neutral language — focus on the work, not the authors. Avoid value-laden adjectives ("terrible," "crazy").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase criticism about 'the work' or 'the data' rather than attacking the authors. Use professional, neutral wording and avoid ad hominem or inflammatory terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise review before submitting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread and edit your review for clarity and tone before sending to the editor; ensure recommendations and comments are coherent and complete.
